title:
Comment of Benjamin Pinkert in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/28/2026

documents.name: 151882.txt
documents.text:
Benjamin Pinkert, Newington, CT.
I oppose DeepGreen's proposed 100-megawatt underwater data center in Cook Inlet, Alaska (Docket P-15423-000). The project would span 1,400-1,650 offshore acres near Nikiski, including up to 350 tidal turbines, 66 subsea data-center pods, and a 3.5-mile underwater cable, within NOAA-designated critical habitat for Cook Inlet beluga whales. Only about 331 of these whales remain, down from roughly 1,300 in 1979. Belugas depend on sound to communicate, navigate, find food, and detect danger, so added underwater noise and construction in their habitat risk hearing impairment, separation of family groups, and loss of prey or habitat. FERC should evaluate this project against the cumulative stressors these whales already face, not in isolation. I urge FERC to reject this project outright. At a minimum, it must not move forward without a full review of cumulative noise, habitat loss, and the other stressors facing this critically small population.
